extraction_warnings: This paper reports aggregate/subgroup-level data (control, pHTN, HTN) for a human cohort of 196 individuals; no per-participant (sample-level) rows are given in the provided text.
Several demographic details (age, sex counts, some clinical parameters) are referenced as being in supplementary Table S1, which is not included in the provided text.
The pmid field was populated from the paper_id metadata rather than from in-text evidence, since PMID is not stated in the body text.

The animal experiment (fecal transplantation into germ-free mice) constitutes a separate sub-study with its own control/HTN mouse groups, which were not treated as separate schema subgroups here since the schema focuses on human participant-level metadata.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Control', 'pHTN', 'HTN'] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pHTN', 'HTN']; kept batch 0.

This study is about hypertension/gut microbiome, not a cancer, twin, neonatal, or reproductive health study; many schema fields (zygosity, tumor staging, RECIST, neonatal fields, obgyn fields, HLA) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

fmt_role field required introducing subgroup labels (FMT Donor, FMT Recipient mice) that differ from the main study subgroups (Control/pHTN/HTN) used for granularity; downstream users should reconcile these separately.
BMI and age are mentioned as covariates analyzed for correlation with microbiome composition but exact values are only in supplementary Table S1, not reproduced in the provided text.
smoker and antibiotics_current_use values were derived from exclusion criteria rather than directly stated as participant-level yes/no fields.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['control', 'pHTN', 'HTN']; kept batch 0.

Schema fields (biomarker_name/value/unit, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size fields) appear designed for oncology/clinical trial studies and are largely not applicable to this hypertension/microbiome study; marked as not_reported.

host_species field only allows a single string, but the paper involves two host species (human participants and germ-free mice for FMT experiments); only 'human' was selected as primary, with mouse use noted separately.

Many quantitative details (e.g., clinical biomarker values, genus abundance levels) are referenced as being in supplementary tables (Additional files) not included in the provided text, limiting full extraction of biomarker fields.
